summary: The analysis component is the engine's retrieval and search substrate for the perceive stage. It runs three tiers over code: a BM25Index for lexical keyword search, a VectorStore of embedded CodeChunks (via Mock/TfIdf/Http EmbeddingBackends) searched through an HNSW VectorIndex for semantic recall, and a CodeGraph / WorkspaceGraph of GraphNodes and GraphEdges for structural traversal. An ErrorAnalyzer classifies compiler errors into fixes, and a DebtPrioritizer quantifies tech debt. On the loop it is how the agent finds the right code: chunk, index, search, filter, rank, then feed grounded results into reasoning.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed with src/analysis/ read in the context of the full engine under a ~600k budget framing; hybrid lexical/semantic/structural retrieval assumes a large codebase whose relevant slices must be surfaced without loading everything.

examples.title: Chunk source files before indexing anything
examples.intent: Break code into retrievable units with metadata so every index has something coherent to hold.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The chunker splits files into CodeChunks (functions, structs, modules) with ChunkMetadata (path, line range, ChunkType), giving the perceive stage the atomic units all three search tiers index.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a file node onto the chunker splits it into a fan of labeled chunk tiles by symbol.
touch_interaction.visual: The file bursts into chunk tiles, each color-tagged by ChunkType (Function blue, Struct green, Test amber).

examples.mini_scenario: The user drags analyzer.rs onto the chunker and it fans into function and impl chunks, each stamped with its line range.
examples.pitfall: Chunk boundaries must preserve line ranges accurately; a chunk whose metadata lines drift makes every later search result cite the wrong location.

examples.title: Build a BM25Index for lexical keyword search
examples.intent: Enable fast exact-term retrieval over symbol names and documented words.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: BM25Index tokenizes chunks (splitting camelCase and snake_case), builds term frequencies and IDF, and gives the perceive stage O(fast) keyword lookup with k1/b tuned scoring.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the lexical node triggers an index rebuild; term buckets fill and the IDF table settles.
touch_interaction.visual: A word-cloud of terms condenses into an index grid; the k1/b tuning knobs sit on the node's rim.

examples.mini_scenario: The user long-presses to rebuild BM25 after new files land, and 'getUserName' tokenizes to get/user/name for retrieval.
examples.pitfall: The IDF and avgdl must be recomputed on rebuild; searching a stale index after documents changed scores terms against outdated frequencies.

examples.title: Embed chunks into the VectorStore with a backend
examples.intent: Turn code chunks into vectors so meaning-based recall becomes possible.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorStore generates embeddings via the chosen EmbeddingBackend (Mock, TfIdf, or Http) and L2-normalizes them into the VectorIndex, arming the perceive stage for semantic search.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a chunk sends it through the embedding pipeline; a vector trail flows into the HNSW node.
touch_interaction.visual: The chunk emits a shimmering vector arrow that threads into the index sphere, which pulses as it inserts.

examples.mini_scenario: With the Http backend configured, the user taps a batch of chunks and their embeddings stream into the HNSW index.
examples.pitfall: Embedding dimension must match the index; feeding vectors from a different backend dimension into an existing VectorIndex corrupts search.

examples.title: Search the VectorIndex for the k nearest chunks
examples.intent: Retrieve the chunks whose meaning is closest to the query, not just its words.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorStore.search embeds the query and runs HNSW k-NN with ef_search, returning SearchResults (chunk, score, distance) that the perceive stage folds into context.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading from the query node radiates a similarity field; the nearest chunk tiles pull toward it.
touch_interaction.visual: Chunks arrange by distance in concentric rings; the closest glow bright, distant ones fade with rising distance labels.

examples.mini_scenario: A query about retry logic returns the three nearest chunks by cosine similarity even though none contain the word 'retry'.
examples.pitfall: Score is 1 minus HNSW distance; treating raw distance as relevance inverts the ranking and surfaces the least similar chunks.

examples.title: Apply a SearchFilter to scope results
examples.intent: Restrict search to relevant files, chunk types, languages, or a min score.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A SearchFilter (file patterns, ChunkType, language, tags, min_score) narrows the result set before ranking, so the perceive stage only ingests chunks that pass the scope.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the results panel opens filter chips; toggling one dims out chunks that fail the scope.
touch_interaction.visual: Filter chips (Function, *.rs, score>0.5) light when active; failing chunks grey out and drop from the stack.

examples.mini_scenario: The user filters to Function chunks in src/ with score above 0.6, cutting a noisy result set to five precise hits.
examples.pitfall: A min_score set too high can empty the result set; over-filtering starves reasoning of context it needed to answer.

examples.title: Weight results by ChunkType before final rank
examples.intent: Prefer higher-signal chunk kinds when two results score similarly.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChunkType.weight (Function 1.0, Import 0.3...) multiplies raw similarity, so the reason stage ranks a matching function above a matching import at equal cosine.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the ranking dial re-weights by type; function tiles climb the list while imports sink.
touch_interaction.visual: Tiles reshuffle as their weight badges apply; the list reorders with a smooth vertical slide.

examples.mini_scenario: Two chunks tie on similarity; the type weight lifts the Function above the Comment so it ranks first in context.
examples.pitfall: Type weight should nudge, not dominate; over-weighting can bury a highly relevant comment that actually answers the query.

examples.title: Combine BM25 and vector scores into a hybrid rank
examples.intent: Get the precision of keyword match plus the recall of semantic similarity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The reason stage fuses BM25Results with vector SearchResults, so a chunk strong on either exact terms or meaning surfaces, widening what the loop can find.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the lexical and semantic result columns together merges them into one fused ranking.
touch_interaction.visual: Two colored streams (blue lexical, green semantic) braid into a single ranked column with blended tile borders.

examples.mini_scenario: A query for 'BM25' hits exactly via lexical and its neighbors via semantic; fusion returns both the definition and its callers.
examples.pitfall: Normalize the two score scales before fusing; adding raw BM25 to cosine lets one metric silently swamp the other.

examples.title: Soft-delete a chunk and defer compaction
examples.intent: Remove a stale chunk from results without an expensive index rebuild.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorIndex marks the entry deleted and filters it from results, letting the control layer defer compaction until the deletion ratio crosses its threshold.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a chunk tile off the canvas marks it deleted; it greys but stays in place until compaction sweeps.
touch_interaction.visual: The tile fades to a ghost outline; a deletion-ratio meter on the index ticks up toward the compaction line.

examples.mini_scenario: A refactored function's old chunk is flicked out; it vanishes from results while the index waits to compact past 30%.
examples.pitfall: Compact when the deletion ratio crosses its threshold; letting soft-deleted entries accumulate unbounded bloats the index and slows search.

examples.title: Scope collections by Project, Session, or Global
examples.intent: Keep chunk sets separated so search targets the right lifetime of code.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorCollection groups CodeChunks by scope (Project, Session, Global) and persists across restarts, letting the foundation layer route search to the correct persistence tier.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the store cycles the active collection scope; the chunk pool visibly swaps.
touch_interaction.visual: A scope tab (Project/Session/Global) highlights; the tile pool underneath fades out and swaps to the scoped set.

examples.mini_scenario: The user double-taps to the Session collection so search returns only chunks from this working session, not the whole project.
examples.pitfall: Searching the wrong scope misleads; querying Global when the answer lives in the Session collection returns stale project-wide code.

examples.title: Classify a compiler error into an AnalyzedError
examples.intent: Turn raw compiler output into a categorized, prioritized error the loop can act on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ErrorAnalyzer pattern-matches output into an AnalyzedError with an ErrorCategory (TypeError, BorrowError...) and priority, giving the perceive stage structured signal instead of a wall of text.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a raw error line classifies it into a category chip and slots it by priority.
touch_interaction.visual: The error line snaps a category badge (BorrowError red, StyleWarning grey) and drops into a priority-ordered lane.

examples.mini_scenario: A cargo build fails; the analyzer tags an E0502 as BorrowError at high priority so recovery addresses it before a style warning.
examples.pitfall: Category drives priority; misclassifying a blocking TypeError as a StyleWarning lets the loop skip past a fatal error.

examples.title: Emit a FixSuggestion with a confidence and auto-fix flag
examples.intent: Propose a concrete fix and mark whether it is safe to apply automatically.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A FixSuggestion (description, fix_code, confidence, auto_fixable) lets the reason stage decide between auto-applying a high-confidence fix and routing a risky one to review.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing an error reveals its fix card with a confidence meter and an auto-fix toggle.
touch_interaction.visual: The fix card unfolds; a green auto-fix badge shows when auto_fixable, the confidence bar filling proportionally.

examples.mini_scenario: An unused import gets a high-confidence auto_fixable suggestion, applied silently, while a lifetime fix routes to review.
examples.pitfall: Only auto-apply when auto_fixable and confidence are high; auto-applying a low-confidence structural fix can compile away real intent.

examples.title: Build the CodeGraph of entities and edges
examples.intent: Represent the codebase as a DAG so structural queries become possible.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph assembles GraphNodes (File, Function, Struct...) linked by GraphEdges (Calls, Imports, Implements...), giving the foundation layer a traversable structure beside the text indices.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading over the codebase node expands it into a live node-and-edge graph laid out by dependency.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes settle into a force-directed layout; Calls edges thin blue, Imports dashed, Implements bold arrows.

examples.mini_scenario: The user spreads the graph and sees the call structure of the analyzer module render as connected function nodes.
examples.pitfall: Edge weights and types must reflect real relations; a fabricated Calls edge corrupts every path query built on the graph.

examples.title: Find a path between two GraphNodes
examples.intent: Discover how one code entity reaches another through the dependency structure.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph.find_path runs BFS over GraphEdges between two GraphNodes, giving the reason stage the concrete chain linking a caller to a callee.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing from one node to another traces the shortest edge path; the route highlights hop by hop.
touch_interaction.visual: A glowing path lights the intermediate nodes and edges; off-path nodes dim to focus the route.

examples.mini_scenario: The user draws from a public API node to a private helper and the graph highlights the three-hop call chain between them.
examples.pitfall: BFS finds a shortest path, not the only one; presenting it as the sole route hides other dependency chains that also matter.

examples.title: Detect cycles in the CodeGraph
examples.intent: Flag circular dependencies that signal fragile architecture.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph.find_cycles surfaces circular GraphEdge chains, letting the verify stage reject or warn on structures that would tangle the dependency order.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the graph runs a cycle sweep; any loop of edges lights red and its nodes pulse together.
touch_interaction.visual: A detected cycle rings its nodes in red and animates the loop direction with a rotating dashed edge.

examples.mini_scenario: The verify stage runs cycle detection before a merge and flags a new A-to-B-to-A import loop for the human to break.
examples.pitfall: A cycle in test-only edges may be acceptable; treating every cycle as fatal blocks harmless mutual references.

examples.title: Summarize the WorkspaceGraph for a focus symbol
examples.intent: Retrieve a bounded structural neighborhood around one symbol of interest.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WorkspaceGraphOptions (focus, neighborhood_depth, max_nodes) build a WorkspaceGraphSummary, giving the perceive stage a size-capped subgraph centered on the focus.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching around a focus node crops the graph to its neighborhood at the chosen depth.
touch_interaction.visual: The graph fades to grey except the focus and its depth-N neighbors, which stay sharp within a lens circle.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches around VectorStore at depth 2 and gets its callers, callees, and their types capped at max_nodes.
examples.pitfall: Respect max_nodes; an unbounded neighborhood around a hub symbol expands to the whole workspace and blows the budget.

examples.title: Identify hub nodes in the CodeGraph
examples.intent: Find the most-connected entities that a change would ripple through.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph ranks GraphNodes by edge degree, so the reason stage knows which entities are high-impact before proposing a change near them.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading on the graph scales each node by its degree; hubs swell large while leaves shrink.
touch_interaction.visual: Node sizes rescale to degree; the biggest hubs glow warm and cast the most edges, leaves shrink to dots.

examples.mini_scenario: The user spreads and sees ProjectIntelligence swell as the largest hub, warning that touching it ripples widely.
examples.pitfall: Degree measures coupling, not importance; a high-degree utility may be safe to change while a low-degree core type is not.

examples.title: Prioritize a DebtItem with the DebtPrioritizer
examples.intent: Rank technical debt so the loop fixes the highest-value items first.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DebtPrioritizer scores each DebtItem by a strategy (RiskImpactEffort, QuickWins, SecurityFirst...), giving the reason stage an ordered debt roadmap.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the strategy selector re-sorts the debt list under the chosen prioritization rule.
touch_interaction.visual: Debt cards re-order; under SecurityFirst the security items jump to the top with a red shield accent.

examples.mini_scenario: The user flicks to QuickWins and the low-effort high-impact debt items rise to the top of the roadmap.
examples.pitfall: The strategy changes the order, not the debt; switching to CostFirst can bury a critical security item that RiskImpactEffort surfaced.

examples.title: Compute compounding cost on a DebtItem
examples.intent: Quantify how a debt item grows in cost the longer it is left.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A DebtItem's interest_rate and age_days compound its total cost, giving the verify stage a hard number that justifies acting now versus deferring.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a debt card unfurls its cost curve rising with age at its interest rate.
touch_interaction.visual: A cost curve arcs upward on the card; the current age marker glows and the projected cost ticks higher as it ages.

examples.mini_scenario: A duplication debt item is long-pressed and its compounding curve shows the cost doubling if deferred another quarter.
examples.pitfall: Interest rate defaults by DebtType; applying a flat rate to every item understates the true cost of high-interest categories like Security.

examples.title: Evict vocabulary when the TfIdf backend overflows
examples.intent: Keep the lightweight embedding backend bounded as the codebase grows.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The TfIdfEmbeddingProvider evicts terms when its vocabulary exceeds MAX_VOCABULARY_SIZE, so the control layer keeps embedding memory bounded without swapping backends.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the overflowing vocabulary panel ejects the least-informative terms off its bottom edge.
touch_interaction.visual: A vocabulary bar hits its ceiling and flashes; rare low-weight terms slough off the bottom as it settles back under the cap.

examples.mini_scenario: As indexing crosses 50k terms, the TfIdf backend evicts the rarest terms so embedding memory stays flat.
examples.pitfall: Eviction drops terms from future embeddings; evicting a term still present in indexed chunks skews their vectors on re-embed.

examples.title: Render the CodeGraph to a shareable diagram
examples.intent: Export the structural graph as a diagram a human can read and reason over.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph renders to DOT, Mermaid, ASCII, or PlantUML, letting the act stage produce a human-facing artifact from the same structure the loop reasons on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the graph exports it to the selected format; a rendered diagram card slides out.
touch_interaction.visual: A format chip (Mermaid/DOT) highlights and a clean rendered diagram peels off the live graph as a shareable card.

examples.mini_scenario: The user double-taps to export the module graph as Mermaid for a design doc, matching the graph the agent searched.
examples.pitfall: Rendering must reflect the current graph; exporting a cached diagram after the graph re-scanned ships a picture that lies about the code.
